extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: Visual Genome is a dataset designed to enable modeling of relationships between objects in images, providing dense annotations of objects, attributes, relationships, region descriptions, and question-answer pairs. It contains over 100K images with an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships per image. The dataset aims to bridge the gap between perceptual and cognitive tasks in computer vision by providing structured representations of images in the form of scene graphs.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.citeAs: Krishna, R., Zhu, Y., Groth, O., Johnson, J., Hata, K., Kravitz, J., Chen, S., Kalantidis, Y., Li, L.-J., Shamma, D. A., Bernstein, M. S., & Fei-Fei, L. (2016). Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv preprint arXiv:1602.07332.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The Visual Genome dataset was collected entirely through crowdsourcing using Amazon Mechanical Turk. Over 33,000 unique workers contributed to the dataset over 6 months, with approximately 800,000 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) launched. Workers were paid $6-$8 per hour, adhering to ethical research standards. The dataset includes 108,249 images sourced from the intersection of MS-COCO and YFCC100M datasets. Each image was annotated with region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs. The collection process involved multiple stages, including region description collection, object extraction, attribute and relationship extraction, scene graph construction, and question-answer pair generation. All annotations were verified through majority voting or rapid judgments to ensure quality.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Crowdsourcing, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of 108,249 real-world images sourced from the intersection of MS-COCO (328,000 images) and YFCC100M (100 million images) datasets. These images are non-iconic, real-world photos uploaded to Flickr by users, covering a wide range of scenes and objects.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The dataset was collected over 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on data representation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The dataset underwent several preprocessing steps, including canonicalization of objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases to WordNet synsets to reduce ambiguity and connect to other resources. This involved mapping terms to their most frequent matching synset in WordNet, with hand-crafted rules for common failure cases. Additionally, region descriptions and question-answer pairs were cleaned, and bounding boxes were verified for coverage and quality. Verification was conducted using majority voting (for most components) and rapid judgments (for objects) to ensure accuracy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were collected through crowdsourcing on Amazon Mechanical Turk. Workers were tasked with writing region descriptions, extracting objects, attributes, and relationships from descriptions, constructing region and scene graphs, and generating question-answer pairs. Workers followed specific guidelines, such as ensuring region descriptions were diverse and not repetitive, bounding boxes covered all mentioned objects, and question-answer pairs started with one of the 'seven Ws' (who, what, where, when, why, how, which). All annotations were verified through majority voting or rapid judgments to ensure quality.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotations were analyzed for quality and diversity. Region descriptions were checked for semantic diversity using word2vec and hierarchical agglomerative clustering. Objects, attributes, and relationships were canonicalized to WordNet synsets to reduce ambiguity. Question-answer pairs were analyzed for type distribution, length, and diversity. Verification processes, such as majority voting and rapid judgments, were used to ensure accuracy.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 42 region descriptions per image on average, with each region description containing an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships. Additionally, each image contains an average of 17 question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The majority of crowd workers were between the ages of 25 and 34 years old, with a near-balanced split of 54.15% male and 45.85% female workers. The youngest contributor was 18 years old, and the oldest was 68 years old. Geographic distribution: 93.02% from the United States, 1.29% from the Philippines, 1.13% from Kenya, 0.94% from India, 0.50% from Russia, 0.47% from Canada, and 2.65% from other countries.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford NLP tools (for noun phrase extraction and dependency parsing), WordNet (for canonicalization of objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases), BLEU score thresholds (for ensuring diversity in region descriptions), and rapid judgments (for verification of objects).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available and maintained by Stanford University. It includes versioning information, with the first release using 108,249 images from the intersection of MS-COCO and YFCC100M datasets. The dataset is designed to be a general-purpose representation of the visual world, enabling research on comprehensive scene understanding.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes descriptions and annotations of people, which may contain sensitive attributes such as gender, age, and clothing. However, the dataset does not explicitly collect or store personal identifiable information beyond what is visible in the images.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance the field of computer vision by enabling models to understand the interactions and relationships between objects in images, which is crucial for tasks like image description, question answering, and robotic interactions. It provides a structured representation of images that can be used for training and benchmarking models for cognitive tasks.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset exhibits biases towards images of people, sports, and certain objects due to the source images from MS-COCO and YFCC100M. Additionally, the canonicalization process may introduce biases based on WordNet's lexeme counts and hierarchy. The dataset also reflects the biases present in the source images, such as a higher representation of certain demographics and activities.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to real-world, non-iconic images and may not capture all possible visual scenarios. The annotations are crowdsourced, which can introduce variability and noise. The canonicalization process, while reducing ambiguity, may not be perfect and can still contain some ambiguity. The dataset may also have limitations in terms of generalization due to biases in the source images and annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine-tuning. The dataset is designed for training and benchmarking models for comprehensive scene understanding, including tasks like object detection, attribute prediction, relationship extraction, region description generation, and visual question answering. It can also be used for semantic image retrieval, attention-based search methods, and as a measurement for image understanding models.
